question: What the rear's placing asks of a held-back division in a battle

addresses.name: CAIUnit_PlaceReserves
addresses.comment: **Held-back divisions to the rear.** 0x4CB840 to the `ret 4` at 0x4CBFE6. Builds a 0x1C record for each province of the second ring +0xA0 (friendly land two steps out) with cap = round(10 x effective infrastructure) (modifier 12 x (1000 + modifiers 13 and 14) / 1000, held between 10 and 1000), counts the held-back divisions into them, then for each held-back division (+0x15C) not retreating (+0x158), not holding ground (CUnit::IsHoldingGround - in a battle whose other side has somebody), with no blocking order (order slot 24 false) and not a garrison (+0x2C9), each refusal the per-unit continue at VA 0x8CBEE5: unless it stands or heads in a ring province within its cap, it is looked at - beside a war candidate's province (IsWarCandidate) across a river or in a fort and fit (strength and organisation above 0.3) it stays; beside war-candidate land units and fit it stays unless our other idle divisions there number at least half of those units; otherwise it goes to the ring province, other than where it is bound, least by map distance + 20 x have - 30 x (its province's depot hops - that province's), with MoveUnit(0, 1, 1). Answers whether it moved one. The name is ours.
addresses.revises: 'not in a battle' made exact: the test is CUnit::IsHoldingGround.
addresses.evidence: VA 0x8CBA93-0x8CBACE: `cmp byte [esi+0x158],0; jne 0x8cbee5`, `push 0; push esi; call 0x5c0160; test al,al; jne 0x8cbee5`, the order's slot 24 (`mov edx,[eax+0x60]; call edx; jne 0x8cbee5`), `cmp [esi+0x2c9],al; jne 0x8cbee5`; VA 0x8CBEE5 increments the index at [ebp-0x2c] and loops to 0x8CBA87. What would show it wrong: 0x8CBEE5 not being the per-unit continue - it is the loop's only increment.
